title: Computer will not connect to Wi-Fi
description: Use basic checks when your computer cannot join a wireless network.
possibleCauses: Wi-Fi is turned off
Airplane mode is on
The saved password is out of date
The router is not available
safetyWarning: Before forgetting a saved network, make sure you know its password. Restarting a shared router briefly disconnects everyone using it. Do not press the router's factory reset button.

steps.instruction: Check that Wi-Fi is turned on and Airplane mode is off in your computer's network settings.
Choose the correct network name and carefully re-enter its password.
Move closer to the router and try connecting again.
If other devices also cannot connect, ask the network owner before restarting the router and modem using their normal power controls.
If the computer still cannot connect, note any message shown and ask your network administrator or internet provider for help.

title: Wi-Fi is connected but internet pages will not load
description: Find out whether the problem affects one computer, one website, or the whole network.
possibleCauses: The internet service is temporarily unavailable
The router has lost its connection
A browser or app is having a problem
safetyWarning: A router restart interrupts other users. Ask first, and use its power control only; do not factory reset it.

steps.instruction: Try opening a different, familiar website or app to check whether only one service is affected.
Check another device on the same Wi-Fi. If it also has no internet, the issue may be with the router or internet service.
Turn Wi-Fi off and back on on the affected computer, then reconnect to the network.
If several devices are affected, ask the network owner to check the modem and router status lights and restart them using the manufacturer's normal instructions.
If the connection remains unavailable, contact the internet provider or network administrator and share which devices are affected.

title: Wi-Fi feels unusually slow
description: Check signal, other devices, and heavy network use before changing router settings.
possibleCauses: Weak signal or obstacles
Several devices are using the connection
A download or stream is using network capacity
A wider service issue

steps.instruction: Move closer to the router and check whether the signal improves.
Pause downloads, cloud backups, or high-quality video streams that you recognize and do not currently need.
Check another device on the same network. If all devices are slow, the cause may be outside this computer.
If practical, test again later and note whether the slowdown happens at particular times or in particular rooms.
If the problem continues across devices, ask the network owner or internet provider to check the connection.

title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting
description: Compare the connection on nearby devices and look for a signal or router pattern.
possibleCauses: Weak or obstructed wireless signal
Low power in a wireless device
A temporary router or computer issue
A network service problem
safetyWarning: Ask before restarting a shared router because it disconnects other users.

steps.instruction: Notice whether the disconnections happen in one room or everywhere, and whether other devices disconnect at the same time.
Move closer to the router and keep the computer away from thick walls and large metal objects where possible.
Turn Wi-Fi off and on again on the computer, then reconnect.
Restart the computer after saving open work.
If several devices disconnect, ask the network owner to check the router or contact the internet provider.

title: One website will not open
description: Check whether the issue is limited to one website, browser, or device.
possibleCauses: The website is temporarily unavailable
The browser needs to be restarted
A browser extension or saved site data is interfering
The address was entered incorrectly
safetyWarning: Do not enter passwords or payment details on a page that looks unexpected or shows security warnings.

steps.instruction: Check the website address for spelling mistakes and try opening a familiar different website.
Close and reopen the browser, then try the address again.
If available, try the same page in another browser you already trust.
Try the page on another device using the same network. This helps tell whether the issue is limited to one computer.
If only that website fails on different devices and networks, contact the website owner or try again later.

title: Computer is running slowly
description: Try simple checks for busy apps, low storage, and pending updates.
possibleCauses: Many apps are open
An app is using a lot of computer resources
The system drive has little free space
The computer needs a restart or update
safetyWarning: Save open work before restarting. Do not end processes or uninstall apps you do not recognize.

steps.instruction: Save your work and restart the computer.
Close apps and browser tabs that you recognize and are not using.
Check the operating system's storage settings to see whether the main drive is nearly full.
Install pending updates using the computer's built-in update settings when you have a stable power and internet connection.
If the computer remains slow, note when it happens and ask your IT support person or device manufacturer for help.

title: An app has stopped responding
description: Give the app a moment, protect unsaved work, and restart it if needed.
possibleCauses: The app is busy with a large task
The app has temporarily frozen
The computer is low on available resources
The app needs an update
safetyWarning: Force-closing an app can lose unsaved changes. Wait first and save work if the app responds again.

steps.instruction: Wait briefly, especially if the app is opening a large file or completing a task.
If the app responds, save your work and close any document or task you no longer need.
If it remains frozen, close it using the normal close control. Use the operating system's force-close option only as a last resort.
Reopen the app and check for an update from its built-in updater or the official store where it was installed.
If the app freezes again, note the file or action involved and contact the app publisher or your IT support person.

title: Computer takes a long time to start
description: Check whether optional apps are slowing startup, while keeping essential security tools enabled.
possibleCauses: Many apps launch automatically
An update is finishing
The computer has limited free storage
A startup app is not responding
safetyWarning: Only disable startup apps you recognize and do not need immediately. Leave security and accessibility tools enabled unless your IT support person advises otherwise.

steps.instruction: Restart once after saving work and note how long startup takes.
Check whether the computer is finishing an operating system update before turning it off again.
Open the operating system's Startup apps settings and review which apps launch automatically.
Turn off automatic startup only for optional apps you recognize. You can still open those apps when needed.
Restart and compare. If startup remains unusually slow, ask IT support before changing advanced startup settings.

title: Main drive is nearly full
description: Find out what is using space and remove only files you know you no longer need.
possibleCauses: Large personal files
Temporary files
A full recycle bin
Many installed apps
safetyWarning: Review files before deleting them. Do not delete operating system folders, files you do not recognize, or items needed by another user.

steps.instruction: Open the operating system's storage settings and review the categories using the most space.
Move personal files you recognize to a trusted backup location if you have one, and check that the copies open before removing originals.
Review the Downloads folder and remove only files you recognize and no longer need.
Review the recycle bin before emptying it, because emptying it permanently removes its contents.
If using the built-in cleanup tool, read its selections before confirming so you understand which files it will remove.

title: Computer feels too hot
description: Reduce blocked airflow and watch for warning signs that need service.
possibleCauses: Air vents are blocked
The computer is under heavy workload
The room or surface is warm
A cooling component may need service
safetyWarning: If you smell burning, see smoke, notice a swollen battery, or the computer becomes painfully hot, turn it off if safe and seek qualified service. Do not open the case or touch internal parts.

steps.instruction: Move the computer onto a hard, flat surface and make sure its outside air vents are not covered.
Close apps you recognize and are not using, then give the computer time to cool.
If the computer shows a temperature warning, shut it down and leave it in a cooler place before trying again.
Do not insert objects into vents or use liquids or sprays on the computer.
If overheating or warning messages return, stop troubleshooting and contact the manufacturer or a qualified repair service.

title: No sound from the computer
description: Check mute, volume, and the selected sound output before changing drivers.
possibleCauses: The computer or app is muted
The wrong output device is selected
Headphones or speakers are disconnected
An app has a sound setting
safetyWarning: Keep volume low when testing headphones, then raise it gradually to protect your hearing.

steps.instruction: Check the computer's volume and mute controls, then check the volume inside the app playing sound.
Check that speakers or headphones are connected and powered on.
Open sound settings and choose the speakers or headphones you intend to use as the output.
Try a different familiar audio app or a short system sound to see whether the issue is limited to one app.
Restart the computer after saving work. If sound is still missing, use the operating system's built-in audio troubleshooter or contact support.

title: Microphone is not working
description: Check mute, connection, selected input, and the app's microphone permission.
possibleCauses: The microphone is muted or disconnected
The wrong input device is selected
The app cannot access the microphone
The microphone level is too low
safetyWarning: Only allow microphone access for apps you recognize and trust.

steps.instruction: Check the headset's mute switch and make sure its cable or wireless connection is in place.
In sound settings, select the microphone you want to use and run the built-in input test if one is available.
Check the operating system's privacy settings and allow microphone access only for the app you intend to use.
Check the app's own audio settings to confirm that the same microphone is selected.
Try the microphone in another trusted app. If it fails there too, use your operating system's audio troubleshooter or ask support.

title: Headphones make crackling or broken sound
description: Check the connection and compare the headphones with another device or app.
possibleCauses: A loose or damaged cable
A poor wireless connection
The audio source or app
An output device setting or driver
safetyWarning: Do not use headphones at high volume to test them.

steps.instruction: Lower the volume, then disconnect and reconnect the headphones firmly.
If the headphones are wireless, move closer to the computer and check that they have charge.
Try a different familiar audio file or app at a low volume.
If possible, test the headphones with another compatible device to help identify whether the issue follows the headphones.
If the sound is still distorted, try another output device or ask the device manufacturer for help.

title: Bluetooth headphones will not pair
description: Check charge, pairing mode, distance, and whether the headphones are connected elsewhere.
possibleCauses: The headphones need charging
Bluetooth is off
The headphones are not in pairing mode
The headphones are already connected to another device

steps.instruction: Charge the headphones and keep them close to the computer.
Turn on Bluetooth on the computer and put the headphones into pairing mode using their instructions.
If the headphones are connected to another nearby device, disconnect them there before trying again.
If they are already listed on the computer, remove that saved pairing and pair them again using the computer's Bluetooth settings.
If pairing still fails, restart Bluetooth on the computer and check the headphone maker's help instructions.

title: Sound plays through the wrong device
description: Select the output you want and check whether the app has its own audio choice.
possibleCauses: A monitor, headset, or speaker became the default output
The app uses a separate output setting
A Bluetooth device connected automatically

steps.instruction: Open sound settings and look at the list of available output devices.
Select the speakers or headphones you want to use and play a short sound at a low volume.
Check the app's sound settings too, because some apps choose an output separately.
Disconnect an audio device you are not using if it keeps becoming the selected output.
If the intended device is missing from settings, reconnect it and use the built-in audio troubleshooter.

title: USB drive is not showing up
description: Check the connection and another port before making changes to the drive.
possibleCauses: The USB plug is not seated
The port or hub is not working
The drive needs power
The computer does not recognize the device
safetyWarning: Do not format, initialize, or erase a drive that contains files you need. Stop if the drive clicks, smells burnt, or becomes unusually hot.

steps.instruction: Remove the drive gently, check for visible damage, then reconnect it without forcing the plug.
Try a different USB port directly on the computer, avoiding an unpowered hub if possible.
If available, try another compatible computer to see whether it recognizes the drive.
If the computer asks to format or initialize the drive, cancel the prompt, especially if it contains important files.
If the drive still is not recognized or has important unreadable files, ask IT support or a data recovery professional before trying repair tools.

title: Computer asks to format a USB drive
description: Protect the files first when a drive appears unreadable or asks to be formatted.
possibleCauses: The file system cannot be read
The drive was disconnected while busy
The drive or its file system may be damaged
safetyWarning: Formatting erases data on the selected drive. Do not format it if you need its files. Do not run repair or recovery tools on the only copy of important data.

steps.instruction: Cancel the format prompt. Do not choose Format, Erase, or Initialize.
Safely eject the drive if the computer allows it, then reconnect it once.
Try another USB port or compatible computer only if doing so will not write changes to the drive.
If the files are important, stop and ask IT support or a reputable data recovery professional about a safe recovery plan.
Only format the drive if you have confirmed that you do not need its contents and have selected the correct drive.

title: Cannot copy a file to a USB drive
description: Check free space, file size, and the connection before trying the copy again.
possibleCauses: The drive is full
The file is larger than the drive's file system allows
The drive connection is unstable
The file is open in another app
safetyWarning: Copy important files rather than moving them, and verify the copied file opens before deleting the original.

steps.instruction: Read the full error message and check how much free space the USB drive has.
Check the file size and make sure the drive has enough free space.
Close the file if it is open in another app, then try copying it again.
Try copying one file at a time and avoid moving the drive during the transfer.
If the error says the file is too large for the format, do not reformat the drive if it contains files you need; ask for help choosing a safe backup and format plan.

title: External drive disconnects during use
description: Check the cable, port, and power while avoiding interruptions to file activity.
possibleCauses: A loose or damaged cable
An unstable USB hub or port
The drive needs more power
The drive or cable may be failing
safetyWarning: Do not unplug a drive while files are being copied or saved. If the drive contains important data or makes unusual noises, stop using it and seek help.

steps.instruction: Wait until no files are copying or saving, then safely eject the drive before checking its cable.
Check the cable and plugs for visible damage. Do not use a frayed or bent cable.
Reconnect the drive directly to another computer port instead of through a hub.
If the drive uses a separate power adapter, check that it is connected as described in the drive's manual.
If disconnections continue, stop repeated testing and ask the manufacturer or IT support to check the drive and cable.

title: USB drive says it is still in use
description: Close files and apps that may be using the drive, then use the system eject control.
possibleCauses: A file on the drive is still open
A copy or save operation is still running
A background app is checking the drive
safetyWarning: Removing a drive while it is being written to can lose or damage files. Do not pull it out while a transfer is active.

steps.instruction: Wait for any visible file copy, save, or backup activity to finish.
Close documents and file browser windows that are open from the USB drive.
Close apps that may be reading or saving files on that drive.
Use the operating system's Safely Remove or Eject option again and wait for its confirmation.
If the computer still says the drive is in use, save your work and shut the computer down normally before disconnecting it.

title: Keyboard is not typing
description: Check power and connection, then test whether only one app is affected.
possibleCauses: Keyboard is disconnected or out of charge
A wireless receiver or Bluetooth connection is unavailable
The app is not accepting input
A key or cable is damaged
safetyWarning: Disconnect a wired keyboard before gently cleaning its outside. Do not pour liquid or spray cleaner into it.

steps.instruction: Click a different text field or app to check whether the problem affects the whole computer.
For a wired keyboard, reconnect it and try another USB port. For a wireless keyboard, check its power and connection.
If it uses a USB receiver, reconnect the receiver directly to the computer instead of through a hub.
Restart the computer after saving work, then test the keyboard again.
If possible, test with another keyboard. If only one keyboard fails, contact its maker or replace it.

title: Mouse or trackpad is not responding
description: Check the pointer device's power, connection, and touchpad setting.
possibleCauses: The mouse battery is low
The cable or wireless receiver is disconnected
The touchpad was turned off
The sensor or surface is obstructed
safetyWarning: Do not open the computer to inspect internal parts. Check the device manual before using any cleaning product.

steps.instruction: For a mouse, check its power or battery and gently clean its outside sensor area with a dry soft cloth.
Reconnect a wired mouse or receiver and try another USB port directly on the computer.
For a laptop touchpad, check the computer's touchpad settings and keyboard touchpad toggle if it has one.
Restart the computer after saving work.
If possible, test another mouse or trackpad. Ask the device maker or IT support if the built-in touchpad remains unavailable.

title: External monitor shows no signal
description: Check monitor power, selected input, cable connections, and display mode.
possibleCauses: Monitor is off or on the wrong input
A cable is loose or damaged
The computer is using another display mode
An adapter or dock is not working
safetyWarning: Do not open the monitor or computer. Never touch exposed connectors or cables that are damaged or hot.

steps.instruction: Check that the monitor is plugged in, powered on, and set to the input used by its cable.
Check that the video cable is firmly connected at both ends. Do not force a connector.
If available, try another compatible cable or connect the monitor directly without a dock or adapter.
Open the computer's display settings and choose a mode that includes the external monitor.
Restart the computer after saving work. If there is still no picture, test with another compatible display or contact support.

title: Webcam is not detected
description: Check the camera cover, privacy permission, connection, and another camera app.
possibleCauses: A privacy shutter is closed
The app lacks camera permission
Another app is using the camera
An external camera is disconnected
safetyWarning: Only allow camera access for apps you recognize and trust.

steps.instruction: Check for a physical camera cover or privacy switch and open it if you want to use the camera.
For an external camera, reconnect it and try a different USB port.
Close video meeting apps that may already be using the camera.
Check the operating system's privacy settings and allow camera access for the app you intend to use.
Test the camera in another trusted app. If it is still missing, use the built-in camera troubleshooter or contact support.

title: Printer will not print
description: Check the printer's power, connection, paper, and selected printer before changing its setup.
possibleCauses: Printer is off or disconnected
The computer selected a different printer
Paper is out or jammed
The printer is paused or has an error
safetyWarning: Follow the printer maker's instructions for clearing a paper jam. Do not pull hard on stuck paper or reach into moving parts. Turn the printer off before checking accessible areas if its manual says to do so.

steps.instruction: Check that the printer is powered on and that its display shows no obvious error.
Check the USB or Wi-Fi connection and confirm the computer and wireless printer use the same network.
Check for paper, ink or toner alerts, an open cover, or a paper jam using the printer's own instructions.
In the print window, confirm that the correct printer is selected and that printing is not paused.
Try a test page or print from another app. If neither works, use the printer's built-in troubleshooter or ask its manufacturer for help.

title: An app will not open
description: Restart the app and computer, then check for a trusted update or repair option.
possibleCauses: The app is already frozen in the background
The app needs an update
The app's local files are damaged
The app is not compatible with this operating system
safetyWarning: Use the app publisher's official website or a trusted app store for updates. Repair or reset options can affect app settings or local data; read the prompt before confirming.

steps.instruction: Wait briefly, then close and reopen the app using its normal controls.
Save other work and restart the computer.
Check for an app update from the official store or the app's built-in update option.
If the operating system offers a Repair option for the app, read what it does and try Repair before Reset or reinstalling.
If the app still will not open, note any error message and contact the app publisher or your IT support person.

title: App installation will not finish
description: Check storage, system compatibility, connection, and the installation source.
possibleCauses: Not enough free storage
The installer does not match the operating system
The internet connection dropped
The app source or installer is not trusted
safetyWarning: Install software only from its official publisher or a trusted store. Do not bypass security warnings or disable antivirus protection to force an installation.

steps.instruction: Read the installation error and write down its wording before closing it.
Check that the computer has enough free storage and meets the app's published system requirements.
If the installer came from the internet, confirm it came from the app publisher's official website or a trusted store.
Restart the computer and try the official installer again when the computer has a stable connection and power.
If installation is blocked by a work or school policy, contact the device administrator instead of trying to bypass it.

title: App update fails or gets stuck
description: Check the connection and storage, then retry through the app's official update channel.
possibleCauses: The internet connection is unstable
The device is low on storage
The update service is temporarily unavailable
The app needs to be closed and reopened
safetyWarning: Keep the computer connected to power during a large update. Do not interrupt an operating system update while it is actively installing or restarting.

steps.instruction: Check whether other websites or apps can connect to the internet.
Check the device's available storage and free space only by removing files you recognize and no longer need.
Close and reopen the app store or the app's built-in updater, then check for the update again.
Restart the computer after saving work, then retry the update from its official source.
If a specific error returns, note its code or wording and check the app publisher's support instructions.

title: A file will not open
description: Check the file name, format, and app before changing or replacing the file.
possibleCauses: No compatible app is installed
The wrong app is selected
The file is incomplete or damaged
The file came from an untrusted source
safetyWarning: Do not change a file's extension to make it open. Only open files from sources you trust, and do not enable macros or other active content unless you know it is safe.

steps.instruction: Check that the file name and location are correct and that the file has finished downloading or copying.
Read the file extension, if visible, and check which app is designed to open that file type.
Use the operating system's Open with option to choose an installed app you trust that supports this file type.
If you have another copy, try that copy without overwriting the original.
If the file is important and still will not open, ask its sender or your IT support person for a fresh copy or the correct app.

title: Unexpected browser pop-ups or redirects
description: Close suspicious pages safely, review browser notifications, and run a trusted security scan.
possibleCauses: A website is showing advertisements
A site was allowed to send notifications
An unwanted browser extension is active
Unwanted software may be present
safetyWarning: Do not call numbers in pop-ups, install a tool they suggest, or provide passwords or payment details. Do not click prompts claiming your computer is infected.

steps.instruction: Do not click buttons or phone numbers in the pop-up. Close the browser tab using its normal close control.
Open the browser's settings and review site notification permissions. Remove permission only for sites you do not recognize or trust.
Review browser extensions and remove only extensions you recognize as unwanted or did not choose to install.
Use the security software already provided by your operating system or a trusted security provider to run a scan.
If redirects continue or you entered sensitive information, stop using the affected browser and contact your IT support or security provider.
